title: Franchise business financing
metaDescription: Franchise businesses often compare SBA 7(a), acquisition financing, term loans, and equipment financing depending on whether the need is a new unit, resale, or buildout. Review the industry-specific documents and fit differences.
summary: The franchise-businesses page explains how franchise-specific disclosure, brand-eligibility, and startup-versus-acquisition differences shape which financing paths tend to fit.

hero.title: Financing a franchise means reviewing the brand documents before you pick the loan.
hero.lead: Franchise borrowers often compare SBA 7(a), acquisition financing, term loans, and equipment financing. The right starting point usually depends on whether the project is a resale, a new unit, or a buildout with equipment and working-capital needs.

quickAnswer.definition: often starts with SBA 7(a), acquisition financing, or term-loan comparisons, because lenders usually need to understand the franchise agreement, the brand's eligibility status, and whether the request covers a purchase, a new opening, or equipment and buildout costs.

whoItFitsHeading: When this industry page fits best
bestFitHeading: Common financing starting points for franchise businesses

bestFitProducts.title: SBA 7(a) loans
bestFitProducts.description: Often part of the first comparison when the franchise request blends startup costs, transfer fees, working capital, or an acquisition.

bestFitProducts.title: Business acquisition financing
bestFitProducts.description: Often relevant when the borrower is purchasing an existing franchise location or buying out an owner rather than opening from scratch.

bestFitProducts.title: Equipment financing
bestFitProducts.description: Worth comparing when the deal includes a meaningful equipment package tied to opening or upgrading the unit.

whoItFits.heading: When franchise-business financing tends to fit
items: Opening a new unit with a franchise agreement, disclosure package, and defined opening budget
Buying an existing franchise location where the deal includes transfer, training, and operating-continuity questions
Projects where brand standards, equipment lists, and required fees shape the total financing need
Borrowers who need to compare one broader loan against a more targeted acquisition or equipment structure

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When this path may not fit as well
items: If the business is not actually operating under a franchise or brand agreement, the broader acquisition or startup pages are usually the cleaner first comparison.
If the primary need is only short-term operating cash after the unit is already open, a working-capital or line-of-credit path may be the better starting point.

underwritingFocusCards.title: Disclosure and agreement package
underwritingFocusCards.description: Franchise requests usually add a disclosure review layer because the FTC's Franchise Rule requires a disclosure document, and lenders often need to understand the franchise agreement and related brand materials.

underwritingFocusCards.title: Brand eligibility and structure
underwritingFocusCards.description: SBA-backed franchise requests often turn on whether the brand appears in the SBA Franchise Directory and whether the project is a new unit, a resale, or another structure under the brand.

underwritingFocusCards.title: Opening budget versus purchase price
underwritingFocusCards.description: Underwriting usually looks different when the ask covers a new-unit opening budget, transfer fees, and equipment rather than the purchase price of an operating location.

typicalDocuments.heading: Common franchise-financing document examples
items: Opening budget or purchase summary showing fees, equipment, and working-capital needs
Brand-eligibility support such as SBA Franchise Directory matching and related business financials if the location is being acquired

commonQuestions.question: What financing paths do franchise businesses commonly compare first?
commonQuestions.answer: SBA 7(a), acquisition financing, term loans, and equipment financing are common starting points, depending on whether the request is for a resale, a new unit, equipment, or a broader opening budget.

commonQuestions.question: Why does the franchise disclosure document matter?
commonQuestions.answer: The FTC's Franchise Rule requires franchisors to provide a disclosure document with specific information, so it often becomes one of the documents borrowers and lenders review early when evaluating a franchise opportunity.

commonQuestions.question: Why does the SBA Franchise Directory come up in financing conversations?
commonQuestions.answer: SBA publishes a Franchise Directory that lenders and CDCs use when evaluating the eligibility of a small business operating under a franchising agreement. That makes brand status part of the early screening for some SBA-backed comparisons.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 approve franchise financing directly?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 does not approve or issue franchise financing directly. Lenders determine eligibility, structure, and terms.
